posts.title: Choosing the Best Dog Food for Hunting Dogs: A Guide to High-Performance Nutrition
posts.excerpt: Discover how to select the best dog food for hunting dogs, focusing on high-performance formulas that meet their unique energy and nutritional needs.
posts.contentHtml:
Understanding the Unique Needs of Hunting Dogs

Hunting dogs are a breed apart when it comes to their nutritional needs. Unlike your average pet, these dogs require a diet that supports high energy levels and intense physical activity. The best dog food for hunting dogs is rich in protein and fat, providing the fuel they need to perform in the field. Protein is crucial for muscle repair and growth, while fats offer a concentrated source of energy. Outlaw Feed is Texas-made with no corn, wheat, or soy — built for exactly these dogs. To see what goes into each bag, read Why Outlaw Feed and our Ingredients breakdown.

What to Look for on the Label

When selecting dog food for hunting dogs, read the label the way a rancher reads a cattle tag:

  • Real, named meat first — not a grain or by-product meal.
  • No corn, wheat, or soy — cheap fillers that dilute protein and add allergen load.
  • Protein and fat matched to workload — higher for hard-working dogs, moderate for family pets.
  • AAFCO-certified for a complete and balanced diet. For instance, a 26/18 formula (26% protein, 18% fat) is ideal for high-drive dogs.

Why 26/18 and 30/20 Formulas Work

Performance formulas like 26/18 and 30/20 are designed for hard-working dogs. The numbers refer to the percentage of protein and fat, respectively. A 30/20 formula is often considered the best 30/20 dog food for hunting breeds, providing the extra energy needed for long days in the field. These formulas help maintain muscle mass and stamina, crucial for bird dogs, hunting hounds, and other active sporting breeds.

Maintenance vs. Performance Formulas

Understanding when to use maintenance versus performance formulas is key. Maintenance formulas suit off-season periods when your dog is less active. During hunting season, a performance formula meets the increased energy demands. Switch between formulas gradually — ideally starting six to eight weeks before peak season — to avoid digestive issues and let your dog adjust.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

One common mistake is relying on cheap fillers that don't provide the necessary nutrients. Overfeeding is another issue; more food doesn't always mean more energy. It's also important not to switch foods too quickly before the season starts, as this can cause digestive upset. Transition to a performance diet over a week or more.

Outlaw Feed Gold and Blue Formulas

Outlaw Feed makes two formulas so you can match the bag to your dog's workload:

  • Gold Formula (High-Performance): 26% protein / 18% fat, built for hard-working ranch, hunting, and sporting dogs that burn through calories in the field.
  • Blue Formula (Adult Maintenance): 21% protein / 15% fat, ideal for active adult and family dogs at a steadier workload. Both are Texas-made with real, named meat and no corn, wheat, or soy.

How Much to Feed and Transitioning

How much to feed your hunting dog depends on their size, age, and activity level. Our Feeding Guide has charts by weight and activity to help you dial in the right amount. When switching to a performance diet, mix the new food with the old over several days so your dog's system can adjust.

Where to Buy Outlaw Feed in Central Texas

Outlaw Feed is stocked at select independently owned farm-supply and feed retailers across Central Texas. Check our store locator for current retailers and addresses. Questions about the closest stocking store? Reach out through our Contact page.

Steadier adult dogs do well on the Blue Formula (21% protein / 15% fat). How do I transition my dog to a new food? Gradually mix the new food with the old over a week or more to avoid digestive upset. For a performance diet, start six to eight weeks before hunting season.
